title: fix(app-shell): the Interfaces pillar's nav rail renders a locale-map label instead of crashing, and resolveSurface resolves it once (objectui#11158)
body:
Fixes #11158

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

The spec types a nav item's `label` as `I18nLabel`: a plain string or an inline locale map. In the Studio's Interfaces pillar:

- `NavTree` rendered the label raw in three places: the group heading, the entry text, and the `title` attribute of an entry with no surface. A map made React throw `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {en, zh-CN})`, and the pillar's whole rail was gone.
- `resolveSurface` read `String(node.label ?? '')` into `Surface.label`, so the canvas caption and the breadcrumb printed `[object Object]`.

## What changed

- **One helper.** `NavTree` reads the heading, the entry text and the `title` attribute through `navItemLabelText(label, locale)` (`previews/navItemLabel.ts`), in the designer locale from `useMetadataLocale()`. It is the helper the canvas card and the nav-item inspector already share. There is no second resolver.
- **`resolveSurface` resolves once.** It takes the locale and carries the resolved text in `Surface.label`. All three callers pass the designer locale: the rail, the first-leaf auto-open in the load effect, and `findSurfaceInTree` behind the `?surface=` restore. `findSurfaceInTree` still matches on `{ type, name }` alone. No `String()` of a label is left in `navSurface.ts`.
- **The type tells the truth.** `NavNode.label` is typed as the spec's `I18nLabel`, so `tsc` refuses a raw render (measured below).
- `locale` is deliberately not a dependency of the load effect. A language switch must not re-run the load, because the load rehydrates the nav edit buffer. A comment at the call says so.

`NavNode`, `Surface`, `resolveSurface` and `findSurfaceInTree` are internal to app-shell. `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` exports none of them, and the package's `exports` map has only `.` and `./styles.css`. So the type change moves no published contract, which matches the claim's `Clause-②: no`.

## Pins

- `StudioDesignSurface.interfacesRailLabelMap-11158.test.tsx` mounts the real `InterfacesPillar` over a mocked metadata client, under en and under zh. Every nav item in the fixture parses against `NavigationItemSchema`. The fixture has a map-labelled first leaf, a map-labelled group, a plain-string leaf (the control), a nested map-labelled leaf, and a map-labelled `url` item. The cases:
  - Every rail row renders: the map labels as their text, the control string as authored. The `url` row is disabled and titled by its text. No `console.error` says "not valid as a React child", and no `[object Object]` appears.
  - The first-leaf auto-open prints the map text in the canvas caption and the breadcrumb.
  - `?surface=page:reports` opens the nested map-labelled leaf, with its caption in the designer locale.
- `navSurface.test.ts`:
  - `resolveSurface` carries the text under `en-US` and under `zh-CN`.
  - A plain-string label is carried as authored (the control).
  - An unlabelled item carries `''`, as before.
  - `findSurfaceInTree` finds the same leaf in both locales.
  - A compile-time `expectTypeOf` pins `NavNode['label']` to `I18nLabel | undefined`.
  - The existing binding cases now pass `LOCALE`.

## Reverse verification (one-time; the fix was committed first)

Each leg changed one anchor through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks the anchor count and the blob hash on disk. It then ran the pin files (or `tsc`) and restored the file. Each restore was proven by a blob equal to `HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`. All legs ran at `e591e1dfd`.

| Leg | Mutation | Predicted | Observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | entry text back to `node.label` | pillar cases red | 6 failed / 30 passed; React logged the card's exact message |
| A2 | `resolveSurface` back to `String(node.label ?? '')` | caption, breadcrumb, restore and unit map cases red; control green | 9 failed / 27 passed (6 pillar cases, 3 unit map cases); the plain-string control stayed green |
| A3 | group heading back to `node.label` | pillar cases red | 6 failed / 30 passed; the same React message |
| A4 | `title` back to `node.label` | only the rows case red | 2 failed / 34 passed |
| T1 | `NavNode.label` back to `string` | `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` red | TS2344 at the `expectTypeOf` pin; TS2322 on the map fixtures |
| T2 | group heading back to `{node.label}` | `tsc --noEmit` red | TS2322: the label type "is not assignable to type 'ReactNode'" |

`tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists both test files (2 of 4802), so the test type-check compiles them. The pillar pin imports the component by relative path from `src/`, so no `dist/` is on its path.

## Verification at `e591e1dfd`

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/`: 156 files and 1532 tests passed, including both pin files.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. Its dependency closure was built first with `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...` (28 of 28 tasks).
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the four changed source and test files: 0 errors. There were 18 warnings before and 18 after, the same set. The load effect's existing `exhaustive-deps` warning now also names `locale`, which is deliberate (see above).
- All passed:
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
  - `pnpm check:control-bytes`
  - `pnpm check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations)
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`
  - `check:test-path-roots`
  - `check:esm-specifiers` (the specifier leg)
  - `check:self-import`
  - `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the five changed paths: NOT GOVERNED
- `check:changeset-claims` (report-only) names one pending changeset, `6681-declared-lazy-marketplace-routes.md`, which cites `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` about its static import of `SuggestedBindingsPanel`. This diff adds no import to that file, so the paragraph still holds.

**Declared narrowing.** The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` belong to CI. The eslint run is narrowed to the changed files, and that narrowing is itself a measurement:

1. The repo config lints all four files: `--format json` returns 4 results, none of them ignored.
2. The resolved config sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware.
3. No rule under `eslint-rules/` reads from disk. A grep for fs reads matches none of them, and the same pattern matches `scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` as a positive control.

So the diff cannot move a lint verdict on a file it does not touch.

**NOT MEASURED**
- `check:eager-closure`, `check:dist-completeness` and `check:published-dist`: they need app-shell's own `dist`. The eager module set is unchanged, but only by reading the code: `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` already imported `navItemLabel.ts` eagerly.
- `check:phantom-deps`: the new import is `@objectstack/spec/ui`. app-shell declares that package (`^17.5.0`), and 76 of its source files already import it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope; measured; same family.** Reported to the seat, not fixed here. The same load effect reads the app's own `label` with `String()`, and `AppSchema.label` is the same `I18nLabel` union. An uncommitted probe on this PR's harness labelled the app `{ en: 'Acme', 'zh-CN': '顶点' }`. The rail heading then read `[object Object] · Navigation` under en and `[object Object] · 导航` under zh. The probe was deleted and the tree is clean. The fix is outside this card's file surface, which covers `NavTree` and the auto-open caller only.
- **Observation; not measured.** `current` holds the Surface as it was resolved when the leaf was opened. After a designer-language switch, the caption and breadcrumb keep the old locale's text until another leaf is picked, while the rail re-resolves on every render. A rename in nav editing leaves the caption stale in the same way, and that part predates this PR. This PR keeps the ruling's "resolves once" design; the note is for whoever next touches the caption.
